land.text: Korea south of the 38th parallel under American administration (infobox: 'American administration south of the 38th parallel: 8 September 1945')

predecessors.note: The American zone had been Japanese Korea until 1945 (empire-of-japan dossier, 1945 loss). Cliopatria starts the Republic of Korea row in 1948.

capitals.name: Seoul
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital and largest city: Seoul'. The 38th parallel was chosen 'as it placed Seoul under U.S. control'; the page does not mention a wartime capital. Seoul was held by the KPA from 28 June to 25 September 1950 and from 4 January to about March 1951 (Korean War page).

keyframe_review.note: 102,811 km2 for 1948-1952: the land south of the 38th parallel ('American administration south of the 38th parallel: 8 September 1945'; 'ROK established: 15 August 1948'). The infobox gives 100,472.4 km2 (today), ratio 1.02. The shape stays on the 38th parallel through the war; the occupation of the South in 1950 and 1951 is carried by ledger events.

104,817 km2 for 1953-2023, 2.0 thousand km2 more than 1948-52. The Korean War infobox: 'A net total of 3,900 km2 changes hand from North Korea to South Korea', 'South Korea gains the city of Sokcho', 'North Korea gains the city of Kaesong'. Cliopatria's diff is 29 cells gained (Gangwon, Gyeonggi) and 13 lost (Hwanghae): net about 4,000 km2, in line with the page. The South Korea infobox gives 100,472.4 km2 (ratio 1.04).
Same outline as 1953-2023 (104,817 km2) against the infobox 100,472.4 km2; 'borders North Korea along the Korean Demilitarized Zone'.

ledger.note: 1948: the Republic of Korea is established in the South. Infobox 'ROK established: 15 August 1948'; 'Rhee won the first presidential elections of the newly declared Republic of Korea in May 1948'. The American administration had governed the zone since 8 September 1945.

region.text: South Korea except 'a corner of southeast Korea, near Pusan' (the Pusan Perimeter), taken by the KPA between 25 June and September 1950

ledger.note: 1950: the North Korean army overruns the Republic of Korea except the Pusan corner. 'On 25 June 1950, North Korea's Korean People's Army (KPA) launched an invasion of South Korea'; 'Seoul was captured by the KPA on 28 June'; 'By September, UN forces were hemmed into a corner of southeast Korea, near Pusan.' The radius around Busan is my reading of the corner.

region.text: South Korea except 'a corner of southeast Korea, near Pusan' (the Pusan Perimeter), taken by the KPA between 25 June and September 1950

ledger.note: 1950: the Inchon landing breaks the North Korean hold on the South. 'On 15 September, UN forces landed at Inchon near Seoul, cutting off KPA troops and supply lines'; 'On 25 September, Seoul was recaptured by UN forces.' The page does not say when the last of the South was cleared, so the month is the recapture of Seoul.

region.text: North Korea, entered by UN and ROK forces in October 1950 and given up in December 1950

ledger.note: 1950: UN and ROK forces cross the 38th parallel and take Pyongyang. 'By 1 October, the UNC had driven the KPA past the 38th parallel'; 'The US Eighth Army drove up western Korea and captured Pyongyang on 19 October'; UN forces advanced 'towards the Yalu River (border with China)'. The page does not say how much of the North was held, so the whole shape is the reading.

region.text: North Korea, entered by UN and ROK forces in October 1950 and given up in December 1950

ledger.note: 1950: the Chinese offensives drive the UN forces out of North Korea. 'UN forces retreated from North Korea in December, following the PVA's first and second offensive'; 'In early December UN forces... evacuated Pyongyang along with refugees.'

region.text: Seoul, captured by the PVA and KPA on 4 January 1951 and lost to a UN counter-offensive two months later

ledger.note: 1951: the Chinese and North Korean armies take Seoul a second time. 'The offensive overwhelmed UN forces, allowing the PVA and KPA to capture Seoul for the second time on 4 January 1951.' The page gives no front line beyond the capital, so the zone is a radius around Seoul.

region.text: Seoul, captured by the PVA and KPA on 4 January 1951 and lost to a UN counter-offensive two months later

ledger.note: 1951: the UN counter-offensive retakes Seoul. 'Communist forces captured Seoul again in January 1951 before losing it to a UN counter-offensive two months later'; 'UN forces retook territory roughly up to the 38th parallel.' March is the page's two months after January.

region.text: the front line of the war of attrition, along what became the Korean Demilitarized Zone

ledger.note: 1951: truce talks begin and the front hardens along what becomes the DMZ. 'Armistice negotiations began in July 1951, but dragged on as the fighting became a war of attrition.' The page gives no front-line positions for 1951-1953, so the zone is a band along the 1953 line (page silent).

region.text: the front line of the war of attrition, along what became the Korean Demilitarized Zone

ledger.note: 1953: the Korean Armistice Agreement ends the fighting. 'Combat ended on 27 July 1953 with the signing of the Korean Armistice Agreement'; it 'created a 4-kilometre wide (2.5 mile) Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) along the frontline'.

region.text: the land south of the front that South Korea gained in the east (Sokcho, Gangwon) in 1953, net 3,900 km2 from North Korea; 'South Korea gains the city of Sokcho'

ledger.note: 1953: the armistice line gives South Korea a strip in the east. Infobox: 'A net total of 3,900 km2 changes hand from North Korea to South Korea'; 'South Korea gains the city of Sokcho'. Cliopatria's 1953 shapes agree: South Korea gains 29 cells (Gangwon, Gyeonggi) and loses 13 in Hwanghae (about 4,000 km2 net).

region.text: the land in Hwanghae, with Kaesong, that North Korea gained in 1953; 'North Korea gains the city of Kaesong'

ledger.note: 1953: South Korea gives up Kaesong at the armistice. Infobox territorial changes: 'North Korea gains the city of Kaesong'; the strip of Hwanghae around it goes with it.

wars.outcome: 'Inconclusive'; the Korean Armistice Agreement of 27 July 1953 created the Korean Demilitarized Zone along the front; 'A net total of 3,900 km2 changes hand from North Korea to South Korea', North Korea gaining Kaesong and South Korea Sokcho.
wars.note: Front by year: 1950 June-September the KPA holds the South down to the Pusan corner; 15 September Inchon landing; October-December UN forces hold Pyongyang and push towards the Yalu (the Chinese enter on 19 October); January-March 1951 the PVA and KPA hold Seoul; spring 1951 the UN line is 'roughly up to the 38th parallel'; July 1951 to July 1953 a war of attrition. The page gives no positions of the front for 1951-1953; the contest zone is a band on the 1953 line. The belligerent list follows the infobox: South Korea and the UN, led by the United States, against North Korea with China and the Soviet Union.

certainty.note: The 38th parallel, the dividing line chosen in 1945 ('as it placed Seoul under U.S. control'), is the northern frontier.
The front line moved across the peninsula (June 1950 to March 1951) and then hardened; no positions for 1951-1952 are on the pages opened.

The armistice of 27 July 1953 created a 4-kilometre Demilitarized Zone 'along the frontline'; the page says South Korea 'borders North Korea along the Korean Demilitarized Zone'. The sea frontier is a coast; the Liancourt Rocks (Dokdo/Takeshima) are disputed with Japan.

notes: Wikidata: Cliopatria's two Korean rows share Q423, the id of North Korea; this dossier keeps Q423 as Cliopatria gives it. They are different states (a southern and a northern government, two Wikipedia articles, two Seshat ids), so no merge: the Republic of Korea is its own dossier and the DPRK another. The Korean War is carried as occupation events (the KPA in the South from June to September 1950, the UN and ROK in the North from October to December 1950, the PVA and KPA at Seoul in January-March 1951), a contest band along the 1953 line from July 1951, and the 1953 gains and losses; the DPRK dossier has the same events with the roles reversed. The pages do not give the front line for 1951-1953. Before 1948: the American administration of 8 September 1945 (infobox) and the Japanese rule before it (empire-of-japan dossier, 1945 loss to the United States) have no dossier in Korea; the owner of the zone is united-states-of-america (am-07). Not on the pages opened: the Liancourt Rocks (Dokdo/Takeshima) are named only as a dispute, with no date; Jeju and the other islands are inside the shape; the page gives no armistice day (the Korean War page does: 27 July 1953); the page does not call Busan a wartime capital. Page budget: two pages (South Korea, Korean War).
